entries.text: Temporal Effectiveness The deviation's power feels slightly stronger (or slightly weaker) at a specific time of day.
Musical Notation Your deviation produces strange ethereal tones or chimes when activated, or you activate it through singing, whistling, or performance.

Strange Biology When you gained your deviation, you grew extra eyes, a set of chitinous antennae, or some other strange biological feature unusual for your ancestry. While you might be able to hide it underneath clothing, your deviant abilities all center around this organ, so it must be uncovered and unobstructed for you to use your deviation.

Chromatic Absorption Whenever you use your deviation, you absorb or mute a specific color from an object near you, and any manifestation of your deviant ability has that color. The absorbed colors return to your surroundings within an hour.
Selective Application The deviation works slightly better (or slightly worse) on a certain type of creature (such as gnomes or caterpillars) or material (such as glass or silver).
Atmospheric Disturbance When you use your deviation, tiny clouds, light wind, or other small atmospheric disturbances occur within 5 feet of your body.
Fractal Sign Your deviation causes sand, droplets, small insects, or other lightweight objects to organize themselves into strange, geometric patterns whenever activated.
Harmless Wound When you use your deviation, trace amounts of blood drip from your eyes or nose.
Strange Fuel Each day, you must consume a small amount of a specific material, such as quartz or holy water (which you can do harmlessly), or your deviation is painful to use.

Forgotten Prayers When you gain your deviation, piecemeal knowledge of a forgotten language fills your mind—not enough to communicate, but enough that you control your deviation by commanding or beseeching some higher power in the language.

Melodic — Faint music plays when in use.
Skin-altering — The user's skin color changes to a bright color such as blue or green.
Choral — Repeats everything the user says in a singing voice.
Mood coloration — User's mood affects the item's color.
Chatty — Happily engages in small talk.
Spoiling — Food within 1 foot spoils at twice the normal rate.
Friendly — Requests to be introduced to everyone the user meets.
Muffling — Nearby sounds are slightly quieter.
Runic — Runes appear on the user's skin.
Comfortable — Can serve as a pillow or blanket.
Rain-blocking — The user remains dry in the rain.
Clumsy — When unattended, knocks over other small items within 1 foot.
Elemental appearance — Seems made of flame, water, or another elemental material.
Magnetic — Small, ferrous objects of light Bulk or less adhere to it.
Aberrant — Has tentacles, teeth, or other off-putting features.
Dream-eating — Creatures asleep within 10 feet do not dream.
Hungry — Needs daily meals, often odd things like wood shavings.
Smelly — Smells like the last food the user ate.
Flamboyant — Flashes of light, sparks of color, and other effects shower from it.
Verdant trail — Small plants grow where the user walks, remaining for 1 hour.
Complaining — Grumbles when not in use.
Detecting — Aware of a specific animal or plant, such as squirrels or poison ivy, within 30 feet.
Fibbing — Tells grandiose and obvious lies.
Attentive — Turns to face the last creature to touch it.
Shrinking — Decreases in size when used.
Temperate — Slight warmth spills from the item.
Slime trail — User leaves a trail of slime where they walk, remaining for 1 hour.
Tetrachromatic — Colors seem more vivid to the user.
Resounding — Nearby sounds are slightly louder.
Insect-attracting — Harmless insects swarm around it.
Ancient tongue — Speaks in a forgotten language.
Bloodthirsty — The sight of blood causes it to quiver in anticipation.
Scribing — Absorbs ink for 1 hour, allowing its points to be used as a pen.
Dirty — A layer of filth always remains.
Preserving — Food within 1 foot spoils at half rate.
Leafy — Small plants grow on or from it.
Wet — It and its user are always damp.
Encouraging — Offers encouragement when the user fails a check.
Loyal — Remains within 5 feet of the user, as if on a tether.
Ritualistic — Demands the user perform a simple act every morning.
Displaced — Appears offset from where it is.
Projecting — Light creates a kaleidoscopic effect.
Taste-altering — Food tastes different, such as tasting sweeter or saltier.
Lucid — Creatures asleep within 10 feet see the item in their dreams.
Decorous — Insists the user use polite language.
Junky — Appears shoddy or made of scraps.
Cavorting — Dances in place when not in use.
Furry — Covered by a thin coat of fur.
Unusually colored — An outlandish color, such as a bright purple suit of armor.
Sonorous — Sounds a pure tone when struck.
Starry — Seems made of night sky.
Compact — Packs neatly into a smaller form.
Misting — Constantly leaking mist or steam.
Chirping — Coos and squeaks when used.
Animal-attracting — Harmless animals follow the user.
Flaunting — Forces user to move dramatically.
Tracing — Followed by thin trails of color.
Monologuing — Recites long lectures or speeches.
Adhesive — Sticks slightly to any surface.
Levitating — Floats slightly above a surface.
Slimy — Covered by a thin layer of slime.
Numbing — User is less sensitive to pain.
Absorbent — Absorbs up to one pint of liquid.
Faceted — Appears made of crystal or gems.
Image-flipping — User appears to be mirrored.
Hair-growing — User's hair grows at double rate.
Sweaty — Becomes damp and pungent when used extensively.
Glittering — Shimmers and glows with light.
Molting — Sheds a thick film every morning.
Echoing — Sounds around the user echo.
Shadowless — Item and user cast no shadow.
Storytelling — Is inscribed with a story or knows a tale it can recite on command.
Chilled — Slightly cool to the touch.
Color-washing — User's vision shifts to a given coloration, such as sepia or monochrome.
Growing — Increases in size when used.
Two quirks — Roll twice on the table and apply both quirks to the item. Reroll any results of 99 or 100.
Three quirks — Roll three times on the table and apply all quirks to the item. Reroll any results of 99 or 100.
Landmark A feature of some significance that distinguishes the hex as noteworthy.
Secret The hex contains a secret the party uncovers upon exploring the hex.
Resource The hex contains some valuable resource appropriate to the terrain.
Standard A standard representation of the terrain type.

Energy Unleashed (evocation) Raw energy deals 2d6 damage per spell level of the surge (basic Reflex save) in a 10-foot burst.

Positive Energy Expulsion (healing, necromancy, positive) Positive energy explodes outward, healing living creatures for 1d8 Hit Points per spell level of the surge in a 20-foot burst. Undead creatures instead take the same amount of positive damage, with a basic Will save.

Mass Siphon (transmutation) Creatures and objects within a 30-foot emanation become nearly weightless until the end of your next turn. Nearly weightless creatures can Climb at their land Speed and can Leap as far upward as they could normally Leap horizontally.

Magical Nemesis (conjuration, teleportation) A random creature connected to your magic (or inimical to it) appears within 60 feet. The creature should be of a level approximately equal to the level of an animal summoned by summon animal of the spell level, although it can be of any type. The GM determines the specific creature. The creature is unfriendly to you and friendly to your apparent enemies. After 1 minute, the creature can choose either to return where it came from or to remain. It is not summoned or a minion.

Monstrous Transformation (mental, morph, transmutation) Your head and arms transform into an exaggerated imitation of a creature connected to your magic for 1 minute. The GM determines the creature. You gain a status bonus to weapon and unarmed damage rolls equal to the spell level. At the start of each of your turns while you are transformed, you must succeed at a Will saving throw or be confused until the start of your next turn. On a critical success, you can choose to end the effect entirely, also losing the status bonus.

Sudden Gale (air, evocation) Weather in a 40-foot emanation is disturbed. Strong winds blow in a random direction for 1 minute. Each creature that starts its turn in the area must succeed at a Fortitude save or fall prone (and be pushed 10 feet on a critical failure), and you must succeed at this save immediately after the surge. Any movement against the wind is 3, or 3 while flying.
Tremor (earth, evocation) The earth trembles in a 40-foot emanation. Each creature on a surface must immediately succeed at a Fortitude save or fall prone. The surface then becomes 3 for 1 minute.

Oppressive Voice (divination, mental, nonlethal) The voice of your muse, your deity, an ancestor, or another appropriate entity suddenly overwhelms your mind. You must attempt a Will saving throw. You take 1d4 mental damage per spell level with a basic Will save. On a failure, you're also stunned 1 (stunned 2 on a critical failure).
Trinket Squall (illusion) Visual illusions of objects related to your magic fall like rain throughout a 40-foot burst for 1 minute, giving concealment in the area. Creatures can attempt to 2.
Antimagic Eruption (abjuration) The surge attempts to counteract a random spell active on you and on each creature within a 10-foot burst.
Mental Broadcast (detection, divination, mental) For 1 minute, everyone within 30 feet of you can hear your surface thoughts.

Verdant Clutch (conjuration, plant) Plants and vines grow from all surfaces within 20 feet, causing all creatures in the area to be immobilized unless they succeed at a Reflex save. The Escape DC is equal to the spell DC.

Tinge of Terror (emotion, enchantment, fear, mental) All creatures within 20 feet are affected by powerful fright. They attempt a Will save, becoming frightened 1 on a failure or frightened 2 on a critical failure.

Strike up the Band (auditory, illusion) For 1 minute, you are followed by orchestral theme music tied to the emotional content of the actions you're performing. This grants you a +2 status bonus to Diplomacy, Intimidation, and Performance checks, a –2 status penalty to Deception checks, and makes certain uses of Stealth virtually impossible. It might have other effects as the GM sees fit.
Life Sap (necromancy) The surge drains your life force and strength. You become drained 1 and doomed 1, and you are enfeebled 2 for 1 minute.

Ablative Barrier (abjuration) Energy forms a protective barrier that ablates slowly as creatures in the area take damage. All creatures in a 40-foot burst gain resistance to all damage equal to double the surge's spell level for up to 1 minute. Whenever a creature applies this resistance, the resistance for all affected creatures reduces by 1. The effect ends for all creatures when it reduces to 0.

Luminous Pests (illusion, visual) Numerous tiny flying creatures formed of bright colorful light, such as bats or hummingbirds, emerge from you, flying in a 30-foot cone. You and all creatures in the cone must succeed at a Will save or be dazzled for 1 minute, or blinded for 1 round and then dazzled for 1 minute on a critical failure.

Emotional Turmoil (emotion, enchantment, mental) A swirl of conflicting emotions overwhelm you from the surging magic. For 1 minute, attempt a DC 11 flat check at the start of each of your turns. On a success, you gain a +2 status bonus to all attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks; on a failure, you take a –2 status penalty to them instead.
Sudden Downpour (evocation, water) Water cascades from above, putting out non-magical fires in a 10-foot burst and attempting to counteract magical fires.

Spell Surge You immediately cast any spell in your repertoire of the surge's spell level or lower (or from your prepared spells or innate spells if you don't have a repertoire but have been forced to generate a wellspring surge). You must choose a spell that takes 3 or fewer actions to cast.
